content: Understanding the importance of community engagement is critical in controlling the spread of Ebola virus disease (EVD). Effective communication strategies must be implemented to educate communities about the disease and its prevention. The following outlines the key principles and procedures for managing contact tracing efforts in EVD outbreaks, as detailed in the CDC-WHO Emergency Guidelines. Purpose of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) The SOPs are designed to define the structure and responsibilities of the Contact Tracing Team, which is tasked with monitoring individuals who have been in contact with confirmed EVD cases. Once an EVD case is identified, a contact list is generated through the investigation process. Each contact on this list is monitored daily for 21 days following their last exposure to the EVD case. If any contact develops symptoms of EVD, they are immediately isolated, referred for testing, and further investigated. These SOPs are based on WHO technical guidance and have been adapted to local contexts to ensure their effectiveness. Human Resource Requirements Lead Epidemiologist: Oversees all operations, including investigations, staff training, and resource mobilization. Field Epidemiologists: Manage the overall performance of contact tracing and assign contacts to supervisors. Supervisors: Provide oversight for 5-10 Contact Follow-Up Teams and ensure daily operations are conducted effectively. Contact Follow-Up Teams: Composed of two members per team, responsible for daily monitoring of assigned contacts. Data Managers: Handle data entry and analysis. Drivers: Provide transportation for field teams. Equipment and Materials Requirements Case and contact definitions. Contact tracing forms. Alcohol-based sanitizers. Reliable communication devices, such as cell phones. Dedicated vehicles for field operations. Daily Operations 1. The Field Epidemiologist meets with Supervisors to distribute an updated contact list. 2. Supervisors meet with Contact Follow-Up Teams to distribute contact tracing forms, review the previous day’s activities, and address areas for improvement. 3. Supervisors and Contact Follow-Up Teams proceed with fieldwork. 4. At the end of the day, the Contact Follow-Up Teams submit their forms to the Supervisor, who synthesizes the data into a summary report. Any missing contacts are reviewed and highlighted. 5. The summary report is sent to the Data Manager and Field Epidemiologist for electronic entry and analysis. 6. The Lead Epidemiologist reviews the data and shares the summary report and analysis with partners. Team Member Responsibilities Lead Epidemiologist Oversees all operations, including monitoring investigations, training staff, and mobilizing resources. Supervises Field Epidemiologists. Provides updates to committee leaders within the Incident Management Framework. Field Epidemiologist Manages the overall performance of contact tracing. Assigns contacts to appropriate Supervisors. Generates the daily contact list, incorporating new contacts. Identifies contacts not followed the previous day as priorities. Supervises data entry and performs data analysis. Supervisor Distributes updated contact tracing forms to Contact Follow-Up Teams daily. Assigns new contacts to teams. Provides field support to teams. Synthesizes data collected by teams into a daily summary report. Ensures tracers visit assigned contacts daily and provide accurate assessments. Ensures contacts not seen the previous day are followed up. Contact Follow-Up Team Establishes trust and rapport with contacts during the first visit. Provides contacts with their telephone number and hotline information, if available. Answers any questions contacts may have during the follow-up process. Meets each contact daily as per the list provided by the Supervisor. Submits completed forms to the Supervisor at the end of daily fieldwork. Immediately informs the Supervisor if a contact develops symptoms. Investigation Team Interviews potential cases and identifies all contacts of a case. Interviews contacts and assesses symptomatic individuals to determine if they meet the case definition. These procedures are essential for the effective implementation and management of contact tracing efforts during an EVD outbreak. They ensure that all contacts are monitored systematically, symptomatic individuals are promptly isolated, and data is accurately collected and analyzed to inform public health responses.
